---
title: "Quarto, R Markdown, Word and PDF output"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup}
library(niceSMD)
d <- example_table1_data()
tab <- nice_SMD_table1(
  d, "group", c("age", "sex", "smoking"),
  group_for_SMD = c("Control", "Treatment"), notes = "short"
)
```

## In a Quarto or R Markdown document

Put the object as the **last expression** of a chunk:

```r
# inside a .qmd or .Rmd code chunk
tab
```

niceSMD registers a `knit_print` method, so `tab` is rendered as a formatted
table (bold variable names, indented levels, footnotes) in HTML, Word, and PDF
output. Printing it at the console gives a plain-text version with the same
structure. The table below is rendered that way:

```{r render}
tab
```

If you assign the result (`tab <- nice_SMD_table1(...)`) the chunk prints
nothing; end the chunk with `tab` to display it. `nice_trial_table1()` results
render the same way.

## Controlling size and fonts

For a different font or size, end the chunk with the flextable instead:

```{r sized}
table1_flextable(tab, font_size = 9, font_family = "Arial")
```

Wide tables (many groups, or trial tables) read better in a smaller font or, in
Word, a landscape section.

## Further styling with flextable

`table1_flextable()` returns an ordinary `flextable`, so any flextable function
applies:

```{r styled}
ft <- table1_flextable(tab)
ft <- flextable::bg(ft, part = "header", bg = "#EAF0F4")
ft <- flextable::color(ft, part = "header", color = "#243746")
ft
```

## Word files

```{r docx, eval = FALSE}
# Standalone Word file
save_table1_docx(tab, "Table1.docx", landscape = TRUE, font_size = 9)

# Or write while building the table
nice_SMD_table1(d, "group", "age", group_for_SMD = c("Control", "Treatment"),
                docx_path = "Table1.docx")

# Export a flextable you modified yourself
flextable::save_as_docx(`Participant characteristics` = ft, path = "Custom.docx")
```

`save_table1_docx()` never overwrites an existing file unless you set
`overwrite = TRUE`. Headers repeat on each page, and a variable's name stays
with its first row.

## PDF output

Table rendering to PDF goes through LaTeX. If flextable's PDF output has font
or package problems on your machine, `table1_kable()` is a lighter alternative
that needs only knitr:

```{r kable, eval = FALSE}
table1_kable(tab)                    # chunk ending: renders in the document format
table1_kable(tab, format = "latex")  # force LaTeX
cat(tab$notes, sep = "\n")           # footnotes are printed separately
```

## Extracting numbers

```{r numbers}
as.data.frame(tab)[1:3, ]            # the display table
tab$smd[, c("label", "smd", "status")]  # unrounded SMDs
```
